body:
The best-documented practitioner workflow, Michael Fritzell's, works like this. Give Claude standing instructions as an equity analyst. Create **one Claude Project per saved prompt**. Then just type a ticker. Use the larger model for complex, multi-step analysis ([Asian Century Stocks](https://www.asiancenturystocks.com/p/how-to-use-claude-for-equity-resear)). The prompts below adapt his library, the steelman-the-bear technique ([Assistly](https://getassistly.co/blog/how-to-use-claude-for-stock-analysis)) and the Indian forensic checklist for an India-plus-US investor. **Always attach the primary documents** (annual reports, the last 8 concall transcripts, investor decks, rating rationales, and a Screener export) or connect a data MCP. Require a citation for every number.

```text
SYSTEM / PROJECT INSTRUCTIONS
You are a skeptical buy-side equity analyst. Use ONLY the documents I attach
or data returned by connected tools. For every number, cite the document and
page/section. If a figure is not in the sources, say "NOT IN SOURCES" — never
estimate silently. Separate FACT (sourced), INFERENCE (your reasoning), and
UNKNOWN. Be brief and concrete.
```

```text
1) BUSINESS & SEGMENTS
Explain [COMPANY]'s business model in simple terms: products, customers,
suppliers, competitors, pricing/contract terms. Build a 10-year table of
segment revenue and segment EBIT. Identify the smallest segment growing
fastest and its share of incremental profit over the last 3 years.
```

```text
2) SECOND-ORDER MIND MAP
Event/theme: [e.g., defence indigenisation / PLI electronics / AI data-centre
capex / competitor X distress]. Map first-, second- and third-order listed
beneficiaries and losers in [India/US]. For each node give: why it benefits,
% of the company's profit plausibly exposed, what would have to be true, and
which public data (order inflows, capacity utilisation, monthly volumes) would
confirm it within 2 quarters. Flag which nodes are already heavily covered.
```

```text
3) FORENSIC ACCOUNTING (India)
You are a forensic accountant using Schilit's Financial Shenanigans. From the
attached annual reports (last 5 yrs), compute and trend: CFO/EBITDA and
cumulative CFO/PAT; debtor, inventory, payable days; CWIP/gross block;
capitalised expenses (R&D, know-how, interest); other income % of PBT; cash +
debt both high (yield on cash); contingent liabilities and guarantees / net
worth; related-party transactions as % of revenue (AS/Ind AS 24 note + AOC-2);
auditor changes, qualifications, emphasis of matter, CARO remarks; promoter
pledge, preferential allotments/warrants; promoter remuneration vs PAT.
Output a red/amber/green table with page citations.
```

`insight:fraud-base-rates` | 2026-11-19 | tickers: - | confidence: verified

Dyck, Morse & Zingales ('How pervasive is corporate fraud?', Review of Accounting Studies 2024) use Arthur Andersen's collapse as a natural experiment: in an average year ~10% of large US public companies commit (alleged) securities fraud (95% CI 7-14%), ~41% misrepresent financial reports (excluding clerical errors), and about two-thirds of frauds go undetected. Fraud destroys ~1.6% of equity value per year (~$830 bn in 2021). An earlier version estimated 15%. Their 2010 Journal of Finance paper ('Who blows the whistle') found detection mostly came from employees, media, analysts and industry regulators, with auditors and the SEC a minority (exact shares unverified here). Implications for a long-term portfolio: (1) with 20-30 holdings, expect 2-3 to have some misreporting at any time -- diversification and position sizing are fraud insurance; (2) audit sign-off is weak evidence; (3) journalists, short sellers, employees and lenders often see it first (Cobrapost/DHFL, FT/Wirecard, Muddy Waters/Luckin, Hindenburg/Nikola, Cooper/WorldCom). In India, add SEBI forensic audits and NSE/BSE surveillance as detectors; SME and small caps likely have higher rates (no reliable estimate).

**Links:** about -> `strategy:position-sizing`, about -> `insight:avoid-ruin`
**Sources:** <https://www.law.nyu.edu/sites/default/files/upload_documents/Adair Morse How Pervasive is Corporate Fraud.pdf> ; <https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s11142-022-09738-5.pdf> ; <https://alphaarchitect.com/gender-bias/>

`insight:flag-high-pe-context` · verified

RULE: a high P/E is benign when (a) a reverse DCF's implied growth is achievable, i.e., growth ~= reinvestment rate x incremental ROIC and the company can keep reinvesting at that rate; (b) the runway (market share, category formalisation, store count headroom) is long; and (c) current EPS is not peak-cycle. It is also benign when EPS is temporarily depressed (Trent at 155x in May 2020 on COVID EPS). EVIDENCE OF BENIGN: DMart 2017-21 (ROCE 20%+, sales +26%/yr, self-funded), Asian Paints/Pidilite/Page at 40-60x for 15 years (ROCE 25-60%), HDFC Bank at 25-35x with ROE 16-20%. WHERE IT TURNS REAL: (1) P/E ~2x the stock's own long median (Asian Paints 117 and Pidilite ~100 in 2021, Page 81 in 2022, DMart ~200 in 2021, Bajaj Finance 121 in 2021) was followed by 4-6 flat years despite EPS growth; (2) growth decelerates or a new competitor arrives (Birla Opus vs Asian Paints, quick commerce vs DMart, LFL slowdown at Trent); (3) price driven by rerating, not EPS (Tesla 2021). India base rate: after runs ending at P/E >= 70, 13 of 15 winners were lower 2-5 years later (insight:india-mb-pe70-exit). PRACTICAL TEST: reverse DCF at today's price; compare required 10-year EPS CAGR with the last 10 years and with reinvestment x ROIC; check P/E vs own 10-year median; ask whether the next 3 years' EPS growth is visible in unit data (stores, subscribers, volumes).

- Public cluster screens are free and widely used → by our own rule ("public screens = no edge") the prior was
  weak; the data now agrees: **no standalone edge** in US $300M–$10B, 2021–2024.
- Useful role: a **research-queue trigger** (a reason to read the 10-K/proxy), not a buy signal. If we want to
  test further, pre-register *one* refined rule and test it out of sample, e.g.: CMP opportunistic-only
  (insider did not trade the same month in the prior 3 years) + buy ≥ 10% of the insider's existing holding +
  ≤ $1B mcap or banks; evaluate on signals 2017–2020 (build) and 2021–2024 (test).
- For India: SEBI PIT disclosures (Reg 7) could be tested the same way — lower coverage there might
  make the signal *more* informative; that is the more promising follow-up.
